A 27-year-old female with localized pain in the left side of the chest, left iliac fossa, pubis, right breast, and belly, rated 8/10 in intensity, and a pain location precision of 6/10.

Guillain-Barré syndrome: Typically involves ascending paralysis.

Spontaneous pneumothorax: Usually presents with sudden onset of chest pain and shortness of breath.

Unstable angina: Severe chest pain at rest.

Acute pulmonary edema: Presents with shortness of breath and cough.

Anaphylaxis: Severe systemic reaction.

Anemia: Usually asymptomatic or mild.

Scombroid food poisoning: Usually involves nausea and vomiting.

HIV (initial infection): Acute symptoms include fever and rash.
